lines.trans: I have fixed boilers, locks, and clocks, madam, but never a piano.
A piano is just honest wood, wool felt, and steel wire, Tariq.
Press the key to the left first so we see how a healthy hammer moves.
Watch C rise smoothly and strike the three strings—clean and bright.
Now press the silent key right next to it.
Look: the key goes down, but the little wooden hammer leans sideways!
Shine the lamp closer—the tiny brass hinge pin slipped half out of the wood!
Wait... nothing is cracked! The damp air thirty years ago only loosened the felt bushing!
Can you seat a tiny pin that small without splitting the beechwood, Tariq?
Give me quiet light, thin tweezers, and dry glue tomorrow morning.
Once that hammer stands straight, Suad can tune the whole middle octave?
Do you have a tuning key in the chest, Tariq? Look in the bottom drawer!

meanings.note: Praises honest natural materials, authentic recipes, or trustworthy character.

examples.text: الخشب الأصيل بيعيش سنين طويلة لو اعتنينا فيه.
examples.trans: Honest solid wood lasts for decades when cared for.

examples.text: قائمة سلمى بسيطة وأصيلة من خيرات البلد.
examples.trans: Salma's menu is simple and authentic, made with local produce.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعطي, بيعطي).

examples.trans: Did the shopkeeper give you a receipt?
Give me the breakfast bag, please.

meanings.note: First person singular pronoun.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Musical interval of eight scale steps.

examples.text: مدام سعاد عزفت نفس اللحن أوكتاف أعلى.
examples.trans: Madam Suad played the same melody one octave higher.

examples.text: الأوكتاف الوسطاني بالبيانو بده دوزان بسيط.
examples.trans: The middle octave on the piano needs a light tuning.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

meanings.note: Form VIII verb used for rising motion, music, or levels.

examples.text: بترتفع المطرقة بهدوء لما تكبس المفتاح.
examples.trans: The hammer rises smoothly when you press the key.
The sound of laughter rose in the courtyard in the evening.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'without', used identically to MSA.

examples.text: شاي أحمر بدون سكر لو سمحتي.
examples.trans: Black tea without sugar, please.
I entered the booking without my glasses!

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Inner lining of a coat or the tiny wool-felt bushing inside a piano hinge.

examples.text: بطانة اللباد جوا المفصلة بدها تبديل بسيط.
examples.trans: The felt bushing inside the hinge just needs a small adjustment.

examples.text: هاد المعطف الشتوي إله بطانة صوف دافية.
examples.trans: This winter coat has a warm wool lining.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'tomorrow' (بكرا الصبح 'tomorrow morning').

examples.text: بكرا الصبح رح نسبق المي الباردة!
examples.trans: Tomorrow morning we will beat the cold water!
We booked a quiet dinner — will you join us tomorrow?

meanings.note: The musical instrument.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Levantine relational adjective formed from تحت ('under/below') + -aani; opposite of فوقاني.

examples.trans: The tuning wrench is in the bottom drawer.

examples.text: نور مسحت الألواح التحتانية للشباك الكبير.
examples.trans: Nour wiped the lower panes of the tall window.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتحرك, بيتحرك).

examples.text: في قطعة معدن تحركت جوا الصندوق!
examples.trans: A piece of metal shifted inside the box!
The car pulled away from the door.

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: The number 30.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

ثبّت.gloss: to fasten; seat firmly; fix in place

meanings.en: to fasten; seat firmly; fix in place
meanings.note: Form II verb meaning 'seat securely / hold steady'.

examples.text: طارق ثبت اللوحة النحاس ببراغي صغار.
examples.trans: Tariq fastened the brass plate with small screws.

examples.text: امسك السلم من تحت وثبته منيح.
examples.trans: Hold the ladder at the bottom and steady it well.

meanings.note: Commonly used preposition for indicating proximity, next to, or beside.

examples.trans: Put a napkin beside every cup.
There is no light beside the bed.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: Life is sweet with kind people.
Never in my life have I seen a prettier view.

meanings.note: Used for the material wood or timber.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Small metal pin, tack, or brass hinge pivot pin.

examples.text: دبوس المفصلة النحاس صغير كتير وبده ملقط.
examples.trans: The brass hinge pin is tiny and requires tweezers.

examples.text: علقت الورقة على اللوح بدبوس صغير.
examples.trans: I pinned the note onto the board with a small tack.

meanings.note: Unvocalised درج covers both daraj ('stairs', masculine collective) and durj ('desk drawer').

examples.trans: Go up the stairs to the second floor.
The big notebook is inside the drawer.

meanings.note: Essential Jordanian word used for giving directions ('go straight') or to mean doing something immediately.

examples.trans: Turn left and walk straight to the bridge.
Walk straight to the end of the street.

meanings.note: Solfege name standard across the Arab world for the note C (دو، ري، مي...).

examples.text: نغمة دو بالبيانو صوتها صافي وواضح.
examples.trans: The C note on the piano sounds clean and clear.

examples.text: بلش اللحن من نغمة دو الوسطى.
examples.trans: The melody begins on middle C.

meanings.note: Levantine musical term (from Ottoman/Persian dūzān) for tuning stringed instruments; مفتاح دوزان is a tuning wrench.

examples.text: البيانو القديم حافظ على دوزانه بشكل مدهش.
examples.trans: The old piano held its tuning remarkably well.

examples.text: لقينا مفتاح الدوزان بالدرج التحتاني للصندوق.
examples.trans: We found the tuning key in the bottom drawer of the chest.

meanings.note: Quadriliteral Levantine verb from دوزان ('musical tuning').

examples.text: مدام سعاد بتدوزن أوتار البيانو كل فصل.
examples.trans: Madam Suad tunes the piano strings every season.

examples.text: دوزنا الأوكتاف الوسطاني وصار صوته صافي.
examples.trans: We tuned the middle octave and its tone came out clear.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برخي, بيرخي).

examples.text: البيوت القديمة بترخي برغي كل أسبوع!
examples.trans: Old houses loosen a screw every week!
Loosen the rope a little, please.

meanings.note: Refers to moisture in the air or dampness in walls.

examples.text: الرطوبة العالية خلت الخشب القديم ينفخ شوي.
examples.trans: High dampness made the old wood swell slightly.

examples.text: بعد ما صلحنا السطح، راحت الرطوبة من الغرفة.
examples.trans: Once we fixed the roof, the dampness left the room.

meanings.note: Opposite of سميك ('thick'); describes thin glass cups, fine lines, or narrow strips.

examples.text: كاسات القزاز الرفيعة حلوة للشاي بالنعنع.
examples.trans: Thin glass cups are lovely for mint tea.

examples.text: رسم رامي خط رفيع بقلم الرصاص.
examples.trans: Rami drew a fine line in pencil.

meanings.note: Hard, fine-grained beechwood (خشب الزان) used for piano actions and café chairs.

examples.text: مطارق البيانو مصنوعة من خشب الزان المتين.
examples.trans: Piano hammers are crafted from sturdy beechwood.

examples.text: كراسي خشب الزان بتعيش عشرات السنين.
examples.trans: Beechwood chairs last for decades.

meanings.note: Used almost universally in the Levantine adverbial phrase بالزبط (biz-zabt, 'exactly / right on').

examples.text: هاد هو اللون الأخضر اللي بدنا إياه بالزبط!
examples.trans: That is the exact shade of green we want!

examples.text: وصل السايق عالباب الساعة تنتين بالزبط.
examples.trans: The driver arrived at the gate at two o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: From سكت, to fall silent: a person who says nothing, or a thing that makes no sound.

examples.trans: Why are you so quiet today? Is something wrong?
The phone has been silent since the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سخانات.

examples.trans: We started the boiler before breakfast.
The boiler room is down in the basement.

meanings.note: Used with بـ (بسلاسة 'smoothly / effortlessly').

examples.text: بعد نقطة الزيت، الباب فتح بسلاسة.
examples.trans: After a drop of oil, the door swung open smoothly.

examples.text: نغمة دو بتطلع وبتنزل بكل سلاسة.
examples.trans: The C key rises and falls completely smoothly.

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسلاك.

examples.trans: The old wire needs a slight adjustment.
We checked the bell wire by the door.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سليمة, plural: سليمين).

examples.trans: Thank goodness your cup is still intact!
All the plates arrived unbroken.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a year.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Geminate transitive verb meaning 'split wood or tear paper'.

examples.text: انتبه لا تشق الخشب الناشف بالمسمار.
examples.trans: Be careful not to split the dry wood with the nail.

examples.text: فتحت الظرف شوي شوي بدون ما أشق الورقة.
examples.trans: I opened the envelope gently without tearing the sheet.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian directions, شمال (shmaal) means 'left' (contrast شَمال shamaal 'north').

examples.trans: Turn left at the street corner.
The key is on the shelf to your left.

meanings.note: Very common adverb in Jordanian Arabic for 'a little bit' or 'slowly'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
Turn the valve slowly and gently.

meanings.note: Describes a pure musical note, clear sky (سما صافية), or clear broth.

examples.text: نغمة البيانو طلعت صافية متل المي.
examples.trans: The piano note rang out crystal clear.

examples.text: انشالله تضل السما صافية طول نهار التنين.
examples.trans: Hopefully the sky stays clear all day Monday.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken Jordanian noun for 'the morning' (الصبح in the morning, كل صبح every morning).

examples.trans: I drink black coffee every morning.
The morning bread is still hot.

meanings.note: Used in expressions like بهالصغر ('this tiny / that small').

examples.text: ما توقعت برغي بهالصغر يوقف مفتاح كامل!
examples.trans: I never expected a screw that tiny to silence a whole key!

examples.text: مع صغر المساحة، الساحة مبينة شرحة ومرتبة.
examples.trans: Despite its small size, the courtyard feels airy and tidy.

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصلح, بيصلح).

examples.trans: I fix pipes and chairs.
Yesterday you fixed the old heater.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صناديق.

examples.trans: The screwdriver is inside the toolbox.
We moved four boxes out of the hallway.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أصواف.

examples.trans: This wool sweater is warm and soft.
A wool blanket is cosy in winter.

ضرب.gloss: to hit; strike; (of a fuse) blow

meanings.en: to hit; strike; (of a fuse) blow
meanings.note: Basic meaning 'to hit'. In everyday Jordanian a fuse or a machine 'hits' when it blows or fails (الفيوز ضرب 'the fuse blew').

examples.trans: The ball hit the window.

examples.text: الفيوز ضرب لما شغلنا الفرن والغسالة مع بعض.
examples.trans: The fuse blew when we ran the oven and the washing machine together.

meanings.note: Colloquial pronunciation of the word for light.

examples.trans: The yellow light beside the bed is warm.
Turn on the light in the hallway, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: طالعة, plural: طالعين).

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading right out!
We are going up to the third floor.

meanings.note: Form II طلّع means both 'look!' (طلّع بالمراية) and 'bring/carry up' (رح أطلّع الشنتة).

examples.text: طلع بالمراية ورا المكتب يا معلم!
examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the desk, boss!
I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: A very common preposition used to indicate location, possession, or presence.

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday carpenter's word (ghira) for wood or craft glue.

examples.text: نقطة غرا خشب ناشف بتثبت اللباد بمكانه.
examples.trans: A dab of dry wood glue holds the felt right in place.

examples.text: سكر علبة الغرا منيح عشان ما تنشف.
examples.trans: Close the glue bottle tightly so it doesn't dry out.

meanings.note: Tempered steel used for piano strings and tools.

examples.text: أوتار البيانو مصنوعة من سلك فولاذ قوي.
examples.trans: Piano strings are made of strong steel wire.

examples.text: هاد المفك راسه فولاذ وما بينحني.
examples.trans: This screwdriver has a steel tip and never bends.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Preposition and adverb for time or sequence meaning 'prior to' or 'before'.

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقدر, بيقدر).

examples.text: بنقدر نقدم زبدة مالحة مع المربى؟
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with jam?

examples.text: ليش ما قدرت تعطيه القطار بإيدك؟
examples.trans: Why could you not hand him the train yourself?

meanings.note: Form II verb used both transitively ('bring the lamp closer') and intransitively ('come closer').

examples.text: قرب الفانوس شوي عشان أشوف القفل.
examples.trans: Bring the lantern a little closer so I can see the lock.
We pulled the chairs closer to the big table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قفال.

examples.trans: The shopkeeper unlocked the padlock in the morning.
We fitted a new brass lock on the closet.

meanings.note: The Amman verb for pressing a button, doorbell or switch.

examples.text: اكبس الزر الأحمر عشان يفتح الباب.
examples.trans: Press the red button to open the door.

examples.text: كبست الجرس مرتين وما حدا فتح.
examples.trans: I pressed the bell twice and nobody opened.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: The main interrogative word for asking about manner or state.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?
Tell me how to find the shop.

meanings.note: Dense wool felt that cushions piano hammers and bushings.

examples.text: لباد الصوف بيخلي صوت البيانو ناعم ودافي.
examples.trans: Wool felt keeps the piano's tone soft and warm.

examples.text: حطينا قطع لباد صغيرة تحت رجلين الكراسي.
examples.trans: We stuck small felt pads under the chair legs.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بميل, بيميل).

examples.trans: Listen when I tilt the box slightly!
The afternoon sun slanted into the courtyard.

meanings.note: Polite everyday Jordanian address for an adult woman or female guest.

examples.trans: Good morning, madam, please come in!
The room is booked under Madam Suad.

meanings.note: Passive participle of شق ('split/crack').

examples.text: الحمد لله الخشب سليم وما فيه إشي مشقوق.
examples.trans: Thankfully the wood is sound and nothing is cracked.
We replaced the cracked cup with a new one.

meanings.note: Used both for a carpenter's hammer and the small felt-covered wooden hammers inside a piano.

examples.text: كل مفتاح بالبيانو بيحرك مطرقة خشب صغيرة.
examples.trans: Every key on the piano moves a small wooden hammer.

examples.text: المطرقة السليمة بتضرب الأوتار وبترجع فورا.
examples.trans: A healthy hammer strikes the strings and rebounds cleanly.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Means both a door key and a mechanic's spanner/wrench (مفتاح حديد iron wrench).

examples.trans: Here is the key to room four.
We have eight brass keys on the board.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مفصلات.

examples.text: حطيت نقطة زيت على مفصلة الباب.
examples.trans: I put a drop of oil on the door hinge.
The brass hinges of the chest are intact.

meanings.note: Fine tweezers for delicate repair work, or small kitchen tongs.

examples.text: طارق طلب ملقط رفيع عشان يمسك الدبوس النحاس.
examples.trans: Tariq asked for thin tweezers to hold the tiny brass pin.

examples.text: البرغي الصغير ما بينمسك إلا بملقط.
examples.trans: That tiny screw can only be picked up with tweezers.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Can refer to objects lacking moisture or metaphorically to a rude or blunt person.

examples.trans: Here is a dry towel for your coat.
The attic is dry and warm in the rain.

meanings.note: Used for the metal or objects made of it.

examples.trans: We polished the brass keys in the morning.
The brass pot is old and engraved.

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نغمات.

examples.text: سمع كل نغمة من البيانو بهدوء.
examples.trans: He listened quietly to every note of the piano.
The chime of the bell is gentle, not harsh.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنزل, بينزل).

examples.trans: The guests will come down at half past seven.
I came down to ask about the sink water.

meanings.note: Masculine هادي ('quiet') is homographic with the feminine demonstrative هادي ('this'); context and agreement distinguish them cleanly.

examples.trans: The spot above the tree is very quiet.
We prepared the quiet attic room for you.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واضحة, plural: واضحين).

examples.trans: A sincere, clear sentence from the heart.
The address is clear on the card.

meanings.note: Stretched wire or gut string on a piano, oud, or violin.

examples.text: المطرقة بتضرب الأوتار التلاتة فبيطلع صوت صافي.
examples.trans: The hammer strikes the three strings and produces a clear note.

examples.text: كل وتر بالبيانو مشدود بدقة عالية.
examples.trans: Every string inside the piano is tensioned with great precision.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian adjective from وسط ('middle'); pairs naturally with المفتاح الوسطاني and ري الوسطى.

examples.text: المفتاح الوسطاني بالبيانو كان عالق من الرطوبة.
examples.trans: The middle key on the piano was stuck from dampness.

examples.text: الطاولة الوسطانية بالساحة بتاخد أحلى شمس.
examples.trans: The middle table in the courtyard catches the nicest sunshine.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقف, بيوقف).

examples.trans: A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate!
My heart stopped at page one!

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!
